expr: NWC Ratio = Net Working Capital/Total Assets

name: Cash Conversion Cycle
expr: CCC = Days Inventory Outstanding + Days Sales Outstanding − Days Payable Outstanding

name: Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO)
expr: DIO = (Average Inventory/Cost of Goods Sold) × 365

name: Days Sales Outstanding (DSO)
expr: DSO = (Average Accounts Receivable/Total Credit Sales) × 365

name: Days Payable Outstanding (DPO)
expr: DPO = (Average Accounts Payable/Cost of Goods Sold) × 365

name: Working Capital Turnover Ratio
expr: WC Turnover = Net Sales/Average Working Capital

name: Economic Order Quantity (EOQ)
expr: EOQ = √(2DS/H), D = annual demand, S = ordering cost, H = holding cost per unit

name: Merger vs Acquisition (concept)
expr: a merger combines two companies into one new entity; an acquisition is one company taking over another

name: Synergy (M&A) (concept)
expr: the added value created when two merged companies perform better together than separately

name: Exchange Ratio (M&A)
expr: Exchange Ratio = Offer Price per Share of Target/Share Price of Acquirer

name: Accretion vs Dilution (M&A) (concept)
expr: a deal is accretive if it increases the acquirer's EPS, and dilutive if it decreases it

name: Due Diligence (concept)
expr: a thorough investigation of a target company's finances and operations before completing a deal

name: Hostile Takeover (concept)
expr: an acquisition attempt made directly to shareholders against the wishes of the target's management

name: Click-Through Rate (CTR)
expr: CTR = (Number of Clicks/Number of Impressions) × 100

name: Conversion Rate
expr: Conversion Rate = (Number of Conversions/Total Visitors) × 100

name: Cost Per Click (CPC)
expr: CPC = Total Ad Spend/Number of Clicks

name: Cost Per Mille (CPM)
expr: CPM = (Total Ad Spend/Total Impressions) × 1000

name: Return on Ad Spend (ROAS)
expr: ROAS = Revenue from Ads/Cost of Ads

name: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
expr: CAC = Total Sales & Marketing Cost/Number of New Customers Acquired

name: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)
expr: CLV = Average Purchase Value × Purchase Frequency × Customer Lifespan

name: Bounce Rate
expr: Bounce Rate = (Single-Page Visits/Total Visits) × 100

name: SWOT Analysis (concept)
expr: evaluates a business's Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats

name: Porter's Five Forces (concept)
expr: analyzes industry competitiveness through Rivalry, Supplier Power, Buyer Power, Threat of Substitutes, Threat of New Entrants

name: PESTLE Analysis (concept)
expr: evaluates macro-environmental factors: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental

name: BCG Matrix (concept)
expr: classifies business units as Stars, Cash Cows, Question Marks, or Dogs based on market growth and share

name: Competitive Advantage (concept)
expr: an attribute that allows a company to outperform its competitors, e.g. through cost leadership or differentiation

name: Value Chain Analysis (concept)
expr: examines each business activity to identify where value is added and costs can be reduced

name: Balanced Scorecard (concept)
expr: a strategic performance framework measuring financial, customer, internal process, and learning perspectives

name: Blue Ocean Strategy (concept)
expr: creating uncontested market space rather than competing in an existing, saturated industry

name: Organizational Culture (concept)
expr: the shared values, beliefs, and practices that shape how members of an organization behave

name: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs (concept)
expr: a motivation theory ranking human needs: Physiological, Safety, Social, Esteem, Self-Actualization

name: Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory (concept)
expr: distinguishes hygiene factors (prevent dissatisfaction) from motivators (create satisfaction) at work

name: Employee Turnover Rate
expr: Turnover Rate = (Number of Employees Who Left/Average Total Employees) × 100

name: Span of Control (concept)
expr: the number of subordinates a manager can effectively supervise

name: Transformational vs Transactional Leadership (concept)
expr: transformational leaders inspire change through vision; transactional leaders motivate through rewards and structure

name: Gross Salary vs Net Salary (concept)
expr: gross salary is total earnings before deductions; net salary is what remains after taxes and deductions

name: Overtime Pay Calculation
expr: Overtime Pay = Overtime Hours × (Hourly Rate × Overtime Multiplier)

name: Provident Fund Contribution (concept)
expr: a retirement savings scheme where both employer and employee contribute a percentage of salary regularly

name: Gratuity Calculation (concept)
expr: a lump-sum benefit paid to an employee based on years of service and last drawn salary

name: Cost to Company (CTC)
expr: CTC = Gross Salary + Employer's Contributions (PF, insurance, bonuses, etc.)

name: Compensation Benchmarking (concept)
expr: comparing a company's pay structure against industry standards to remain competitive

name: Sales per Square Foot
expr: Sales per Sq Ft = Total Sales/Total Retail Floor Area (sq ft)

name: Stock-to-Sales Ratio
expr: Stock-to-Sales Ratio = Value of Inventory/Value of Sales

name: Sell-Through Rate
expr: Sell-Through Rate = (Units Sold/Units Received) × 100

name: Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI)
expr: GMROI = Gross Margin/Average Inventory Cost

name: Footfall Conversion Rate
expr: Conversion Rate = (Number of Transactions/Total Footfall) × 100

name: Average Transaction Value
expr: ATV = Total Sales Revenue/Number of Transactions

name: Shrinkage Rate (Retail)
expr: Shrinkage Rate = (Recorded Inventory − Actual Inventory)/Recorded Inventory × 100

name: Same-Store Sales Growth
expr: Growth % = (Current Period Sales − Prior Period Sales)/Prior Period Sales × 100

name: Critical Path (concept)
expr: the longest sequence of dependent tasks in a project, which determines the minimum possible project duration

name: Total Float (Slack)
expr: Total Float = Late Start − Early Start (or Late Finish − Early Finish)

name: PERT Expected Time
expr: TE = (O + 4M + P)/6, O = optimistic, M = most likely, P = pessimistic time

name: PERT Variance
expr: Variance = ((P − O)/6)²

name: Earned Value (EV)
expr: EV = % Complete × Budget at Completion (BAC)

name: Cost Variance (CV)
expr: CV = Earned Value (EV) − Actual Cost (AC)

name: Schedule Variance (SV)
expr: SV = Earned Value (EV) − Planned Value (PV)

name: Cost Performance Index (CPI)
expr: CPI = EV/AC

name: Schedule Performance Index (SPI)
expr: SPI = EV/PV

name: Estimate at Completion (EAC)
expr: EAC = BAC/CPI

name: Capacity Utilization Rate
expr: CUR = (Actual Output/Maximum Possible Output) × 100

name: Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)
expr: OEE = Availability × Performance × Quality

name: Cycle Time
expr: Cycle Time = Net Production Time/Number of Units Produced

name: Takt Time
expr: Takt Time = Available Production Time/Customer Demand

name: Just-in-Time (JIT) (concept)
expr: a production strategy that minimizes inventory by receiving goods only as they are needed in the process

name: Six Sigma (concept)
expr: a data-driven methodology aiming to reduce process defects to 3.4 per million opportunities

name: Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) (concept)
expr: a maintenance approach aiming for zero breakdowns and zero defects through proactive equipment care

name: Throughput
expr: Throughput = Total Output/Total Time

name: Bottleneck (concept)
expr: the process step with the lowest capacity, which limits the overall throughput of a system

name: Lean Manufacturing (concept)
expr: a systematic approach to minimizing waste while maximizing productivity in production processes

name: Consumer Decision-Making Process (concept)
expr: problem recognition → information search → evaluation of alternatives → purchase decision → post-purchase evaluation

name: Brand Loyalty (concept)
expr: the tendency of a consumer to consistently purchase the same brand over competing options

name: Perceived Value
expr: Perceived Value = Perceived Benefits/Perceived Costs

name: Net Promoter Score (NPS)
expr: NPS = % Promoters − % Detractors

name: Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT)
expr: CSAT = (Number of Satisfied Customers/Total Respondents) × 100

name: Maslow's Hierarchy in Consumer Motivation (concept)
expr: consumers seek to satisfy physiological, safety, social, esteem, and self-actualization needs through purchases

name: Cognitive Dissonance (concept)
expr: the discomfort a consumer feels after a purchase when doubting whether it was the right decision

name: Word of Mouth (WOM) Effect (concept)
expr: the influence of informal recommendations and opinions shared between consumers on purchase decisions

name: 7 Cs of Communication (concept)
expr: Clarity, Conciseness, Concreteness, Correctness, Coherence, Completeness, Courtesy

name: Communication Process Model (concept)
expr: sender → encoding → message → channel → decoding → receiver → feedback

name: Barriers to Communication (concept)
expr: factors such as noise, language differences, or perception that distort or block a message

name: Formal vs Informal Communication (concept)
expr: formal communication follows official organizational channels; informal communication (grapevine) flows unofficially

name: Verbal vs Non-verbal Communication (concept)
expr: verbal communication uses spoken or written words; non-verbal uses body language, tone, and gestures

name: Active Listening (concept)
expr: fully concentrating on, understanding, and thoughtfully responding to a speaker's message

name: Total Quality Management (concept)
expr: a management approach focused on continuous improvement of quality across all organizational processes

name: PDCA Cycle (concept)
expr: Plan-Do-Check-Act, a continuous improvement cycle used in quality management

name: Kaizen (concept)
expr: a Japanese philosophy of continuous, incremental improvement involving all employees

name: Cost of Quality
expr: Cost of Quality = Cost of Conformance + Cost of Non-Conformance

name: Defects Per Million Opportunities (DPMO)
expr: DPMO = (Number of Defects/(Units × Opportunities per Unit)) × 1,000,000

name: Quality Control vs Quality Assurance (concept)
expr: quality control detects defects in the finished product; quality assurance prevents defects in the process

name: Benchmarking (concept)
expr: comparing a company's processes and performance metrics against industry best practices

name: Fiscal Policy (concept)
expr: government use of spending and taxation to influence overall economic activity

name: Budget Deficit
expr: Budget Deficit = Total Government Expenditure − Total Government Revenue

name: Fiscal Deficit
expr: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Revenue (excluding borrowings)

name: Public Debt to GDP Ratio
expr: Debt-to-GDP = (Total Public Debt/GDP) × 100

name: Progressive vs Regressive Tax (concept)
expr: progressive tax rates rise with income; regressive tax takes a larger percentage from lower incomes

name: Value Added Tax (VAT) (concept)
expr: a tax levied on the value added at each stage of production or distribution of goods and services

name: Government Subsidy (concept)
expr: financial assistance provided by the government to support a particular industry or activity

name: Crowding Out Effect (concept)
expr: increased government borrowing that reduces private sector investment by raising interest rates

name: Money Supply (M1, M2, M3) (concept)
expr: measures of the total money in circulation, ranging from most liquid (M1) to less liquid (M2, M3)

name: Money Multiplier
expr: Money Multiplier = 1/Reserve Ratio

name: Quantity Theory of Money
expr: MV = PQ, M = money supply, V = velocity, P = price level, Q = output

name: Repo Rate (concept)
expr: the rate at which a central bank lends short-term funds to commercial banks

name: Open Market Operations (concept)
expr: a central bank buying or selling government securities to control the money supply

name: Inflation Targeting (concept)
expr: a central bank policy of setting a specific inflation rate as its explicit monetary policy goal

name: Liquidity Trap (concept)
expr: a situation where very low interest rates fail to stimulate borrowing, spending, or investment

name: Velocity of Money
expr: V = (P × Q)/M

name: Price Elasticity of Demand
expr: Ed = %Δ Quantity Demanded/%Δ Price

name: Income Elasticity of Demand
expr: Ei = %Δ Quantity Demanded/%Δ Income

name: Cross Elasticity of Demand
expr: Exy = %Δ Quantity Demanded of X/%Δ Price of Y

name: Elasticity of Supply
expr: Es = %Δ Quantity Supplied/%Δ Price

name: Marginal Utility
expr: MU = ΔTotal Utility/ΔQuantity Consumed

name: Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility (concept)
expr: each additional unit consumed yields less satisfaction than the previous unit

name: Consumer Surplus (concept)
expr: the difference between what consumers are willing to pay and what they actually pay

name: Producer Surplus (concept)
expr: the difference between what producers receive for a good and the minimum amount they would accept

name: Indifference Curve (concept)
expr: a curve showing combinations of two goods that give a consumer equal satisfaction

name: Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS)
expr: MRS = ΔY/ΔX, measured along an indifference curve

name: GDP — Expenditure Approach
expr: GDP = C + I + G + (X − M)

name: Gross National Product (GNP)
expr: GNP = GDP + Net Income from Abroad

name: Nominal vs Real GDP (concept)
expr: nominal GDP is measured at current prices; real GDP is adjusted for inflation

name: GDP Deflator
expr: GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP/Real GDP) × 100

name: Unemployment Rate
expr: Unemployment Rate = (Number of Unemployed/Labor Force) × 100

name: Inflation Rate
expr: Inflation Rate = ((CPI this year − CPI last year)/CPI last year) × 100

name: Consumer Price Index (CPI) (concept)
expr: measures the average change over time in prices paid by consumers for a basket of goods and services

name: Multiplier Effect
expr: Multiplier = 1/(1 − MPC), MPC = Marginal Propensity to Consume

name: Phillips Curve (concept)
expr: illustrates an inverse relationship between the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment

name: Balance of Trade vs Balance of Payments (concept)
expr: balance of trade covers only goods and services; balance of payments covers all economic transactions with the world

name: Capitalization Rate (Cap Rate)
expr: Cap Rate = Net Operating Income/Current Market Value

name: Gross Rent Multiplier (GRM)
expr: GRM = Property Price/Gross Annual Rental Income

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LTV)
expr: LTV = (Loan Amount/Appraised Property Value) × 100

name: Net Operating Income (NOI)
expr: NOI = Total Rental Income − Operating Expenses

name: Occupancy Rate
expr: Occupancy Rate = (Occupied Units/Total Units) × 100

name: Cash-on-Cash Return
expr: Cash-on-Cash Return = Annual Pre-Tax Cash Flow/Total Cash Invested

name: Property Appreciation Rate
expr: Appreciation Rate = ((Current Value − Purchase Value)/Purchase Value) × 100

name: Actuarial Science (concept)
expr: the discipline applying mathematical and statistical methods to assess risk in insurance and finance

name: Premium Calculation (concept)
expr: the process of determining an insurance premium based on risk probability and expected claims

name: Expected Loss
expr: Expected Loss = Probability of Loss × Amount of Loss

name: Risk Pooling (concept)
expr: spreading risk across a large group so that the losses of a few are covered by the contributions of many

name: Value at Risk (VaR) (concept)
expr: estimates the maximum potential loss of a portfolio over a given time period at a given confidence level

name: Loss Ratio
expr: Loss Ratio = Incurred Losses/Earned Premiums

name: Combined Ratio (Insurance)
expr: Combined Ratio = Loss Ratio + Expense Ratio

name: Behavioral Economics (concept)
expr: studies how psychological, social, and emotional factors influence economic decision-making

name: Anchoring Bias (concept)
expr: the tendency to rely heavily on the first piece of information encountered when making decisions

name: Loss Aversion (concept)
expr: the tendency to prefer avoiding losses over acquiring an equivalent gain

name: Prospect Theory (concept)
expr: describes how people choose between probabilistic alternatives, weighing potential losses and gains differently

name: Herd Behavior (concept)
expr: the tendency of individuals to mimic the actions of a larger group, especially in financial markets

name: Nudge Theory (concept)
expr: using subtle policy shifts to encourage people toward decisions that are in their broad self-interest

name: Game Theory (concept)
expr: the study of strategic decision-making between rational players whose outcomes depend on each other's choices

name: Nash Equilibrium (concept)
expr: a state where no player can improve their outcome by changing strategy while others keep theirs unchanged

name: Prisoner's Dilemma (concept)
expr: a game illustrating why two rational players might not cooperate even when cooperation is in their best interest

name: Dominant Strategy (concept)
expr: a strategy that yields the best outcome for a player regardless of what the other player chooses

name: Zero-Sum Game (concept)
expr: a situation where one player's gain is exactly balanced by another player's loss

name: Cooperative vs Non-Cooperative Game (concept)
expr: cooperative games allow binding agreements between players; non-cooperative games do not

name: First-Mover Advantage (concept)
expr: the competitive edge gained by the first company to enter a market or introduce a product

name: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) (concept)
expr: a company's commitment to conducting business in a way that is ethical, sustainable, and beneficial to society

name: Triple Bottom Line (concept)
expr: evaluates business performance across three dimensions: People, Planet, and Profit

name: Business Ethics (concept)
expr: the study of moral principles that guide decision-making and conduct within a business

name: Code of Conduct (concept)
expr: a set of formal rules outlining the expected behavior and ethical standards for employees of an organization

name: Stakeholder Theory (concept)
expr: holds that a business should create value for all stakeholders, not just shareholders

name: Sustainability Reporting (concept)
expr: the practice of publicly disclosing a company's environmental, social, and economic performance

name: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) (concept)
expr: a set of criteria used to evaluate a company's environmental impact, social responsibility, and governance practices

name: Whistleblowing (concept)
expr: the act of an employee reporting illegal or unethical conduct within an organization to internal or external authorities

name: Conflict of Interest (concept)
expr: a situation where a person's personal interests could improperly influence their professional judgment or duties

name: Fair Trade (concept)
expr: a trading partnership that ensures fair prices, decent working conditions, and sustainable practices for producers
